body.objective: Students will be able to improve tone with breath support.
body.iCan: I can improve tone with breath support.
successCriteria: I can use full, supported breaths when playing
I can produce a steady, characteristic tone
I can assess my tone with a tuner and recordings
body.hook: Two students play the same note on the same instrument. One sounds thin and wobbly; the other sounds full and steady. The difference usually isn't the instrument; it's air. In high school band, great tone starts with great breath support.

study.title: Air Is Everything
study.question: How does breath support create a great tone?
study.passage:
Part 1, Breathing (5 minutes): Sit tall at the front of the chair. Breathe in for 4 counts, low and full, like filling a glass of water from the bottom. Exhale on a steady "hiss" for 8 counts, then 12, then 16.
Part 2, Long tones (15 minutes): Play concert F (or a comfortable note) for 8 counts at mezzo-forte. Keep the sound steady: no wobbles, no fading at the end. Then try:
• 4 counts crescendo + 4 counts decrescendo
• 8 counts at piano (soft but still supported)
• Long tones on the concert B♭ scale, one note per breath
Percussion: play rolls and single strokes with an even sound at each dynamic, focusing on stroke height and relaxed grip.
Part 3, Listen and measure (10 minutes): Play a long tone with a tuner. Watch the needle: is it steady? Record yourself on a phone and listen back. Compare with a professional recording of your instrument.
Part 4, Ensemble (10 minutes): The full band plays a concert B♭ chorale slowly, listening across the room to match tone and blend.
Daily goal: 5 minutes of long tones at the start of every practice.
